Series::bitwise_and¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::bitwise_and(const Series& rhs) const -> Series

What It Does¶

bitwise_and() combines two integer-like or boolean Series values bit by bit.

For each aligned position, the result bit is 1 only when that bit is 1 in both inputs. That makes bitwise_and() the “keep only the overlap” operator of the bitwise family.

On ordinary integers, that means the operation works on the stored binary representation, not on numeric magnitude in the arithmetic sense. On booleans, the same operation behaves like boolean conjunction, but it stays in the bitwise family and follows bitwise dtype rules.

Parameters¶

rhs (const Series&)

The right-hand operand.

Load-bearing behavior:

  • rhs must be broadcast-compatible with self

  • both operands must have integer or boolean dtype

  • floating-point operands are rejected instead of being silently reinterpreted

Returns¶

Series A new Series whose values are the bitwise overlap of self and rhs.

The result shape follows normal broadcasting. The result dtype follows the library’s integer/boolean promotion rules for the participating operands.

Examples¶

Example 1. Basic integer masking keeps only the bits shared by both operands.

auto left = pluss::make_series({1, 6, 12, 10}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
auto right = pluss::make_series({3, 10, 5, 12}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);

pluss::series::print(std::cout, left.bitwise_and(right));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 4, 8]

The lane-by-lane binary picture is:

  • 1 & 3 -> 0001 & 0011 = 0001

  • 6 & 10 -> 0110 & 1010 = 0010

  • 12 & 5 -> 1100 & 0101 = 0100

  • 10 & 12 -> 1010 & 1100 = 1000

Example 2. Floating-point inputs are not accepted.

try {
  auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
  auto b = pluss::make_series({1.0, 0.0});
  std::cout << a.bitwise_and(b);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

bitwise: dtype must be integer/bool

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • This is not arithmetic multiplication and not logical short-circuiting.

  • Floating-point dtypes fail fast.

  • Broadcasting still applies, so shape mistakes surface as broadcast errors before the bitwise kernel runs.

Summary¶

Use bitwise_and() when the question is “which bits survive in both inputs?”

See Also¶

  • Series::bitwise_or: keeps bits that appear in either operand.

  • Series::bitwise_xor: keeps bits that differ.

  • Series::logical_and: truth-value logic rather than raw bit patterns.
